text:
I wasn't in this situation but know a lot of people from this situation from moderating the group etc. 

1. During the war, tourists were not allowed to enter on rescue flights, but there were generally no problems for an Israeli residents (including those on A5/B1 visas) to return to Israel, so long as they have a valid visa and intervisa. Many many foreigners in mixed couples did return, including alone. I heard of a very small number of instances of airline staff challenging the foreigner's right to come back on 'rescue flights', but in all cases they were allowed to board after saying/proving that they lived in Israel. Your husband should bring his ID card with him when he travels, just in case he needs to prove he lives in Israel. 

3. If the situations gets so bad that El Al cancels flights, it is very likely that PIBA offices will close and cancel appointments anyway, and we would be likely to see another round of automatic visa extensions. Even if the visa does not get automatically extended (because your husband is abroad), you should be able to get home (probably using an ETA), and then you would need to go to PIBA once it reopens to get a visa and a new appointment. Many couples had to go through this last time - it is not a big drama, and it is not the end of the world if your husband is in Israel without a visa for a couple of weeks because of the war 🙂
